title: Free SD Card Photo Recovery for Mac — CardMe
description: Photos won’t open, accidentally deleted them, or formatted your SD card? Try CardMe, a free JPEG photo recovery app for Mac. No account needed. Never writes to your card.
heading:

lead: Photos won’t open, accidentally deleted them, or formatted your card? CardMe helps you find what can still be recovered, without writing to the card.
steps: Use a working card reader, then select your card in CardMe to start scanning.
Click “Rescue to…” and choose a folder on your Mac or another drive for the recovered photos.
See which photos were recovered at full size, which have only a preview or thumbnail, and which could not be recovered.
warningTitle: Stop using the card for now
warning: Don’t take more photos or save new files to it. They could overwrite photos you might still be able to recover.
faq: Do I have to pay to save recovered photos?
No. Scanning, recovery and saving are all free, with no account required. Donations are optional.
Can I recover photos after deleting them or formatting the card?

Try Deep Rescue. It makes a complete copy of the card, then looks for JPEG data left after deletion or a quick format. Intact data stored in one continuous piece may be recoverable. The result depends on what remains on the card.
Will CardMe change anything on my card?
CardMe only reads the card. It does not write to it, format it or repair it. Copies and recovered photos are saved to another drive. macOS and other apps may still read or write to the card.
What do I need for Deep Rescue?
A working card reader and enough storage: more free space than the card’s stated capacity for the complete copy, plus room for recovered photos. Bigger cards take longer to copy.
RAW photo recovery and overwritten data are currently not supported. Photos split across separate parts of the card cannot generally be reassembled. Sometimes only a preview or thumbnail remains.

No. Photo recovery takes place on your Mac. Usage statistics are enabled by default; you can turn them off in CardMe → Settings → Privacy. Photos, filenames, paths and card details are never uploaded. The website counts visits and clicks on download and support links without cookies or persistent identifiers. It respects Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control. The hosting service still receives connection information such as IP addresses.
How does Deep Rescue find photos?

It looks for JPEG markers in the complete card copy, checks the file structure and image data boundaries, then checks whether each photo can be decoded before saving it. A photo that opens may still have visible damage, so please check the results.
Why did it only find a preview or thumbnail?

Cameras may save smaller previews alongside the full-size photo, including thumbnails in EXIF. These can remain even when the full-size image is damaged. CardMe labels them separately. It does not enlarge small images to pass them off as originals or generate missing image content.
Can EXIF recover the original filename?

EXIF usually records when a photo was taken, the camera details and its orientation. Filenames are usually stored in the card’s file system and may be lost during formatting. Some cameras record file numbers in MakerNote metadata, but the format varies by model. A number alone does not always identify the original filename.
